title: Ian McKeever explores light, transparency, and time in new Heather Gaudio exhibition
summary: Heather Gaudio Fine Art is presenting Ian McKeever: Going Forth, Painted Panels & Other Works, the artist’s third solo exhibition at the gallery. The show runs through December 5th. Ian McKeever is an acclaimed British artist whose distinguished career is marked primarily as an abstract painter. He works serially, simultaneously developing several paintings that take several years to complete. Each series is characterized with its own identity, inspired by nature, art history or culturally historic works, and all share the artist’s preoccupation with light, transparency and the bodily presence. The two predominant series featured in the exhibition are the new Going Forth paintings and the continuing Painted Panels which the artist began in 2012. title: AV17 Gallery brings Žilvinas Kempinas to Artissima 2026
summary: This autumn, (AV17) Gallery , Vilnius, brings the work of internationally acclaimed Lithuanian artist Žilvinas Kempinas to Artissima 2026, one of Italy’s leading contemporary art fairs. The presentation will explore Kempinas’ distinctive approach to movement, perception, light and space, transforming familiar materials and physical forces into dynamic, often unexpectedly immersive visual experiences. Based in New York since 1997, Kempinas has developed a practice that occupies a distinctive position between sculpture, installation and perception-based art. Magnetic tape, light, air, gravity and other seemingly simple elements become active participants in his work, producing situations that change according to the viewer’s movement and the surrounding environment. title: Luhring Augustine announces representation of Leon Kossoff Estate
summary: Luhring Augustine announced representation of the Estate of Leon Kossoff, in collaboration with Annely Juda Fine Art, London, and Xavier Hufkens, Brussels. Earlier this year (April-June 2026), in partnership with the Estate, Luhring Augustine staged a major exhibition of Kossoff’s paintings that spanned the artist’s career. Andrea Rose, Art Historian and Editor of the Leon Kossoff catalogue raisonné and Dr. Barnaby Wright, Deputy Head of the Courtauld Gallery and the Daniel Katz Curator of 20th Century Art, served as co-curators of the exhibition. One of the most substantial presentations of the artist’s work to be held in New York in recent decades, the exhibition was accompanied by a fully illustrated catalogue featuring a specially commissioned essay by acclaimed critic Hilton Als. Leon Kossoff (1926–2019) was a leading figure of postwar British art, who was celebrated for his deeply expressive paintings and drawings of the people and places that shaped his life.

title: Thyssen-Bornemisza and Mauritshuis swap iconic 17th-century works in unprecedented partnership
summary: The Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza and the Mauritshuis in The Hague are simultaneously exchanging twenty-five outstanding works from their permanent collections thanks to a collaboration agreement between the two institutions. In Madrid, an exceptional collection of 17th-century Dutch masterpieces is on display, including Johannes Vermeer's View of Delft (ca. 1660-1661), brought together in the classical rooms, a new exhibition space in the museum, close to the rooms dedicated to this same school, thus offering a more complete view of that extraordinary and fruitful century. The Thyssen-Bornemisza family's ties to the Netherlands date back to the early 20th century, when Heinrich (1875–1947) settled in The Hague after the Hungarian Revolution of 1919. title: The Frick Collection presents groundbreaking survey of Sienese Renaissance bronzes
summary: This fall, The Frick Collection presents the first ever exhibition to focus on Siena as a center of artistic excellence and technical innovation in bronze sculpture during the Italian Renaissance. Siena: The Art of Bronze, 1450–1500 brings together nearly forty works—including statues, reliefs, candelabra, medals, and more—by some of the most influential sculptors in this period, among them Donatello, Vecchietta, and Francesco di Giorgio. Owing to their size and importance, many of these objects have never been shown outside of Tuscany, let alone in the United States. Building on popular past presentations of bronze sculpture at the Frick, the exhibition invites visitors to appreciate the medium’s extraordinary beauty and versatility while discovering the technical ingenuity, collaboration, and political ambition behind Sienese bronzework. title: Art of the Islamic and Indian Worlds including Rugs and Carpets at Christie's on 12 November
summary: Christie's much anticipated bi-annual auction of Art of the Islamic and Indian Worlds including Rugs and Carpets will take place on 12 November, celebrating over a millennium of artistic production across the Islamic world and the Indian subcontinent. Comprising over 230 lots, the sale features a selection of manuscripts, paintings, ceramics, metalwork and textiles, highlighting the creativity and craftsmanship of cultures stretching from Spain and North Africa to India and Central Asia, led by an exquisite Syrian wooden panel (estimate: £300,000-400,000). title: Josh Lilley opens Celeste Rapone's third solo exhibition with the gallery
summary: Josh Lilley presents How We're Doing, the third solo exhibition by Celeste Rapone (b. 1985, NJ, USA) with the gallery. Educated and living in Chicago but born and raised in New Jersey, Rapone’s paintings are imbued with the formal sophistication of a former Art Institute lecturer and the sensitive observation of a family member and a spouse. Her daily drive to challenge her technical capacity entails no preparatory drawing or sitters- each painting is an opportunity to explore and learn, discovering the purpose of the picture and the characters of the protagonists within it spontaneously. Behind that process of acute variation rests the years of humble repetition and solitude inherent to a committed, daily practitioner; the studio pilgrimages, the perpetual reaching for the blurry purpose of one’s work. title: Michel Rein Paris presents Nino Kapanadze's debut solo exhibition 'Inertia'
summary: For Nino Kapanadze's first solo exhibition at Michel Rein, Paris, the images, forms and questions that have been central to the French-Georgian artist's practice for several years are brought together here along a single trajectory. In these new paintings, abstraction and figuration coexist in such continuities that defy a strictly serial or chronological interpretation, instead revealing an underlying flow of forms and images capable of shifting, transforming and constantly altering the direction of the work. Here, Nino Kapanadze explores the possibilities of painting more deeply, to the point of feeling the need to redefine its language each time. title: MAXXI L'Aquila highlights Fabio Mauri in flagship Italian Capital of Culture 2026 survey
summary: Fabio Mauri: Gli anni dell'Aquila, curated by Maurizio Cattelan and Marta Papini, is an exhibition organised by L'Aquila City Council and produced by MAXXI Museum, and is one of the most eagerly awaited projects as part of L'Aquila's designation as Italian Capital of Culture 2026. The exhibition pays tribute, on the centenary of his birth, to Fabio Mauri an artist, writer and intellectual who was one of the most radical figures of the second half of the 20th century—and is on view at MAXXI L'Aquila until January 24, 2027. The project takes its starting point from the bond that Mauri forged with the city and its inhabitants—from 1979 to 1999, he taught 'Aesthetics of Experimentation' at the Academy of Fine Arts—and explores some of the fundamental themes of his work: the allure of ideologies, the mechanisms of propaganda, the power of images and their ability to influence individual and collective consciousness. title: Briscoe Western Art Museum presents Kathy Sosa's 'Revolutionary Women of Texas and Mexico'
summary: The women who shaped Texas and Mexico were not simply witnesses to history. They were participants, survivors, cultural transmitters, laborers, activists, mothers, revolutionaries and community leaders whose resilience and determination helped shape the cultural landscape connecting Mexico, Texas and the American West. Opening Oct. 15 at the Briscoe Western Art Museum, Kathy Sosa: Revolutionary Women of Texas and Mexico brings those stories to the forefront through more than 30 works by San Antonio artist Kathy Sosa. On view through June 14, 2027, the exhibition complements the Briscoe’s landmark Tejano Legacy: Another American Origin Story and offers a contemporary artistic continuation of the history explored throughout that exhibition. title: The Design Museum offers first look at LAIKA's Wildwood ahead of UK release
summary: The Design Museum has opened LAIKA presents WILDWOOD: The Exhibition, a new exhibition created in collaboration with Portland, Oregon-based stop-motion animation studio LAIKA. The exhibition follows the London premiere of Wildwood, directed by Travis Knight, at the BFI London Film Festival, where the film has attracted widespread critical acclaim from publications including Forbes, The Telegraph and Variety. It opens ahead of the film’s UK and Irish cinema release on 23 October 2026, offering audiences a unique opportunity to explore the design, craft and technology behind LAIKA’s filmmaking before experiencing the finished film on screen. The exhibition marks a significant first for LAIKA, bringing the studio’s creative process to a major public exhibition ahead of the film’s release in cinemas. title: A new dawn for Tarnanthi Festival: Artistic Director and major partnerships announced
summary: Building on ten years of extraordinary artistic and cultural achievement, the Art Gallery of South Australia has unveiled the next chapter of its acclaimed Tarnanthi Festival, announcing Noongar curator and artist Zali Morgan as Artistic Director alongside landmark new funding partnerships. The first program highlights for the 2027 Tarnanthi Festival have also been revealed, including the major survey exhibition Yunupiŋu: Seven Sisters, developed in collaboration with Buku-Larrŋgay Mulka Centre and the Yunupiŋu family; and, Melting Point: Wati Wai!, an ambitious project developed by Mimili Maku Arts and initiated by Yankunytjatjara artist and cultural leader Robert Fielding and the Mimili Maku Wati Studio. Based near Boorloo/Perth, Zali Morgan is a Noongar woman with ancestral connections to Whadjuk, Balladong and Wilman Boodjar. title: Galleri Magnus Karlsson hosts Alejandro Sintura's first international solo exhibition
summary: Galleri Magnus Karlsson announces Alejandro Sintura’s first solo exhibition at the gallery. In Between Hidden and Almost Revealed a series of new paintings are presented. The exhibition’s title is taken from Brazilian author Clarice Lispector’s posthumous novel A Breath of Life (1978), which has been important to the artist during the working process. In an attempt to put into words an almost unbearable beauty, she describes it as something ”Between the hidden and the almost revealed. It’s also a shimmering desperation and the pain gets confused with beauty and mixed with an apocalyptic joy.” In a similar vein, Alejandro Sintura speaks of his paintings—as an attempt to unite form, material, and subject in order to bring something elusive and hard to grasp to light. title: Zayed National Museum announces first exhibition to explore 7,000 years of camel history
summary: Zayed National Museum, the national museum of the UAE, announces its inaugural temporary exhibition, Tracks Through Time: The Camel in Society, Trade and Art. The world’s first exhibition to comprehensively explore more than 7,000 years of camel history will open early December 2026, coinciding with the museum’s first anniversary celebration. Tracks Through Time examines the camel’s role in society, trade networks and creative cultures of the UAE and the wider region, from the earliest evidence of wild camels on this land to the living traditions practised today. title: Alex Müller explores memory, material, and time at Haverkampf Leistenschneider
summary: “One can, and of this I am convinced, only ever begin in the middle.” So begins the autofictional short story “Between July and October,” written by Alex Müller while she was still a student and read aloud in class in 2001. Until 2025, it was never heard or read again. Along with other materials and objects that Müller finds, collects, receives as gifts, dismantles, or rescues, it forms a kind of archive. Like a seed in the ground, this short story waited for a moment when it could come to light again and be transformed by the artist into something else: in this case, a pair of white double-jeans dangling from the wall with four legs over three meters long. They look like birch trunks, and Müller handwritten the entire story from 2001 onto them—like a seemingly endless, obsessive bark of writing. title: Fine Books at Swann to feature standout 19th & 20th century literature
summary: Swann's fall Fine Books auction on Thursday, October 22, features special copies of important books in a spectrum of collecting categories. Collectors of early printed books will find incunabula and post-incunabula, including examples in period bindings, along with sixteenth-century English imprints. Special first edition works of nineteenth- and twentieth- century literature are well represented, with first editions by F. Scott Fitzgerald, Ernest Hemingway, J.D. Salinger, Margaret Atwood, Octavia Butler, Emily Brontë, Bram Stoker, John Steinbeck, David Foster Wallace, Jack Kerouac, J.R.R. Tolkien, and others. title: National Gallery reunites Yinka Shonibare's iconic sculpture with Gainsborough's 'Mr and Mrs Andrews'
summary: For the first time since its creation, Yinka Shonibare’s 'Mr. and Mrs. Andrews without their Heads' (1998) will go on display with the painting which inspired it, Thomas Gainsborough’s Mr and Mrs Andrews (about 1750). Yinka Shonibare and Thomas Gainsborough: A Conversation will take place in the H J Hyams Room at the National Gallery from October 2026. Bringing together these two works on the eve of the 300th anniversary of Gainsborough’s birth, the National Gallery will show Shonibare’s vibrant re-evaluation of a very English depiction of privilege and identity through sculpture. This will mark a once in a generation opportunity to see 'Mr. and Mrs. Andrews without their Heads' in the UK, on loan from the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa. title: Purdy Hicks Gallery presents Omar Fakhoury's solo exhibition 'Two Balconies and One Superstition'
summary: Two Balconies and One Superstition began, quite simply, with Omar Fakhoury looking at the things around him. One balcony is his own, where his bedroom windows look onto a giant rubber tree, which he describes as a kind of living screen, shifting with the light and wind. The other is the Corniche, Beirut’s balcony onto the sea, which he walks often. Here are the palms bending in the wind, the changing sea and sunsets, and the ladders installed by swimmers on the rocks, descending straight into the Mediterranean—as though, for a moment, the whole sea were a swimming pool. The paintings came about in much the same way. Subjects that had been quietly sitting in Fakhoury’s mind were suddenly jolted into being painted. title: Poster Auctions International to sell renowned William W. Crouse Art Deco collection
summary: On October 20, Poster Auctions International (PAI) presents Selling Modernism: The William W. Crouse Collection, an exceptional selection of rare Art Deco vintage posters. Featuring works by A.M. Cassandre, Paul Colin, Charles Loupot, Leonetto Cappiello, Jean Carlu, Roger Broders, Otto Ernst, Edward McKnight Kauffer, and others, the auction spans automobiles, aviation, railways, ocean liners, entertainment, sports, and consumer products. Originally designed for commercial purposes, these once everyday advertisements are now prized collectibles of art historical importance that helped to define graphic design for the rest of the century. Of further note, the majority of the posters in the Crouse Collection are framed with valuable museum-grade acrylic glazing. Assembled by William W. title: Tim Van Laere Gallery presents Tal R's fourth solo exhibition
summary: Tim Van Laere Gallery presents its fourth solo show by Tal R, titled Woman Behind Fence. In this exhibition Tal R presents a new body of sculptures, paintings and drawings that explores figures at the moment they seem to fall out of character — bending, collapsing, hiding and transforming into something that remains deliberately difficult to define. The starting point for the exhibition was an unexpected departure from the artist’s usual way of working. Tal R has traditionally approached painting and sculpture with a fixed plan, beginning with a question or a clear desire. This time, he deliberately did the opposite.
